summary: The UK government says Lithuania follows Schengen area rules, and EU nationals have the right to travel freely there. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (consolidated to 30 December 2025), nationals of the countries in its Annex II are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries in Annex I must hold a visa; the Schengen Visa Code sets the visa fee at EUR 90. The UK government says only one border crossing point between Lithuania and Belarus remains open.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa. tips.text: The UK government says only one border crossing point between Lithuania and Belarus remains open, Medininkai–Kamenny Log, and only by private vehicle, and that Russian-plated vehicles are currently only permitted to enter Lithuania for up to 24 hours if transiting to or from the Kaliningrad Oblast. Canada says Lithuania enforces an EU entry ban on vehicles with Russian or Belarusian licence plates, and that certain exceptions apply.

The UK government says the Curonian Spit is divided between Lithuania and Russia, with the southern half part of Kaliningrad, and that the walk along the Spit in Lithuanian territory will eventually reach Russian territory; Canada says the Nida border-crossing point between Russia (Kaliningrad) and Lithuania is closed.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lithuania?
faq.answer: EU nationals have the right to travel freely in Lithuania. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (consolidated to 30 December 2025), nationals of the countries in its Annex II are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries in Annex I must hold a visa. The EU says ETIAS, the travel authorisation that will be required of visa-exempt nationals, is currently not in operation.

faq.question: Can Russian citizens enter Lithuania?
faq.answer: Lithuania's Foreign Ministry says that under Law No XIV-1888 of 20 April 2023 the acceptance of Schengen visa applications of Russian and Belarusian citizens at Lithuania's visa authorities abroad is suspended, except when the Ministry mediates the application, for example for family members of Lithuanian or EU citizens, or when the trip cannot be postponed. The European Commission says Russian nationals will no longer be able to receive multiple-entry visas.

faq.question: How much does a Lithuania Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: Under the Schengen Visa Code the short-stay visa fee is EUR 90; children from six and below 12 pay EUR 45, and children under six are exempt.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Lithuania?
faq.answer: The EU says ETIAS is currently not in operation, that no applications are collected, and that it will announce the start date several months before launch. It says ETIAS will be an entry requirement for visa-exempt nationals and lists a EUR 20 application fee.

faq.question: Can I cross into Lithuania from Belarus?
faq.answer: The UK government says only one border crossing point between Lithuania and Belarus remains open, Medininkai–Kamenny Log, that crossing is only possible by private vehicle as scheduled buses are not operating, and that Lithuania denies entry to cars registered in Belarus, with certain exemptions.
